unitTitle: Some - Any/Much - Many/A Few - A Little/Phrases of Quantity - Giving Advice - Conditionals Type 0 - Time Words

pairsWith.noteUz: Bu nazariya beti Coursebook 6-unit (Food, Glorious Food) grammatikasini takrorlaydi: some/any, much/many, a few/a little, miqdor iboralari, should, 0-tur shart gap, vaqt so'zlari.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 6-UNIT NAZARIYA + 1-MAShQ (30-bet, PDF 29). Yuqorida chapda ko'k '6', sarlavha: 'Some - Any/Much-Many/A Few - A Little/Phrases of Quantity - Giving Advice - Conditionals Type 0 - Time Words'. Och pushti ramka, ikki ustun.

CHAP USTUN:
'Some - Any': • We use some in the affirmative with countable nouns in the plural and uncountable nouns. 'I want some strawberries and some ice cream.' • We also use some for offers or requests. 'Would you like some orange juice? (offer) Can I have some milk, please? (request)' • We use any in the negative and interrogative form with countable nouns in the plural and uncountable nouns. 'There isn't any salt left. Have you got any biscuits?'
'Much - Many': • We use much and many in questions and negations. Much is followed by uncountable nouns and many is followed by plural countable nouns. 'Is there much sugar in the bag? There isn't much milk in the carton. Have you got many records? She hasn't got many friends.'
'A Few / A Little': • We use a few (= not many, some) with plural countable nouns. 'We've got a few eggs.' • We use a little (= not much, some) with uncountable nouns. 'I want a little orange juice.'
'Phrases of Quantity': • We use countable and uncountable nouns after phrases of quantity such as: a jar/bottle/piece/loaf/cup/bar/glass/kilo/carton/bowl, etc.

O'NG USTUN:
'Giving Advice - Should / Shouldn't': • We use should to say what the right/best thing to do is. 'You should eat plenty of fruit and vegetables. (= It's a good idea)' • We use shouldn't to say what isn't the right/best thing to do. 'You shouldn't eat junk food. (= It isn't a good idea)'
'Conditionals Type 0': • Type 0 conditionals are used to express something which is always true. They are also used to talk about something which always happens as a result of something else. They are formed as follows: If clause: If + present simple → main clause: present simple. 'If the temperature falls below 0°C, water turns into ice.' • In type 0 conditionals we can use when (= whenever) instead of if. 'If/When the sun shines, snow melts.'
'Time Words': • We do not use the future simple after the time words before, after, while, until, as soon as, and when. We use the present simple instead. 'I'll wait for you until you finish. (NOT: I'll wait for you until you'll finish.)' • When can be followed by future simple if it is used as a question word. 'When will he arrive? (when = question word) I can't tell you when it will be ready. (when = question word) Please give me a call when you finish work. (when = time word)'

PASTDA - 'Some - Any / Much - Many / A Few - A Little':
1) 'Fill in the gaps with some or any.' 1 A: Would you like ...... tomato sauce on your spaghetti? B: Yes, please. 2 A: Are there ...... apricots in the fridge? B: No, I'm afraid there aren't ...... . 3 A: Can I have ...... cake, please? B: Of course you can. 4 A: We don't have ...... apple juice. B: I'll go to the supermarket and buy ...... . 5 A: Would you like ...... milk in your tea? B: No, thank you. 6 A: There isn't ...... ice cream in the freezer. B: Are you sure? I thought we had ...... . 7 A: Can I have ...... bread? B: Here you go.

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '30'.

exercises.instructionEn: We use some in the affirmative with countable nouns in the plural and uncountable nouns: I want some strawberries and some ice cream. We also use some for offers or requests: Would you like some orange juice? (offer) Can I have some milk, please? (request). We use any in the negative and interrogative form with countable nouns in the plural and uncountable nouns: There isn't any salt left. Have you got any biscuits?
exercises.instructionUz: 'Some' tasdiq gapda ko'plik sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar bilan ishlatiladi: Men qulupnay va muzqaymoq xohlayman. 'Some' taklif va so'rovda ham ishlatiladi: Apelsin sharbati ichasizmi? (taklif) Sut bera olasizmi? (so'rov). 'Any' inkor va so'roq gapda ko'plik sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar bilan: Tuz qolmagan. Pechenye bormi?
exercises.explanationUz:
SOME va ANY - BIR OZ / BIROR.

  SOME - TASDIQ:
    I want SOME strawberries
    (ko'plik) and SOME ice cream
    (sanalmaydigan).

  SOME - TAKLIF va SO'ROV (savol
  bo'lsa ham!):
    Would you like SOME orange
    juice? (taklif)
    Can I have SOME milk, please?
    (so'rov)

  ANY - INKOR va SO'ROQ:
    There isn't ANY salt left.
    Have you got ANY biscuits?


⚠ SAVOLDA SOME yoki ANY?

  Oddiy savol → ANY (bormi?)
  Taklif / so'rov → SOME ('ha'
  javobini kutamiz)

points.en: I want some strawberries and some ice cream. (affirmative)
Would you like some orange juice? (offer) Can I have some milk, please? (request)
points.uz: Apelsin sharbati ichasizmi? (taklif) Sut bera olasizmi? (so'rov)
points.noteUz: ⚠ Taklif va so'rovda some (savol bo'lsa ham).

points.en: There isn't any salt left. Have you got any biscuits? (negative and interrogative)
points.uz: Tuz qolmagan. Pechenye bormi? (inkor va so'roq)

exercises.instructionEn: We use much and many in questions and negations. Much is followed by uncountable nouns and many by plural countable nouns: Is there much sugar in the bag? There isn't much milk in the carton. Have you got many records? She hasn't got many friends. We use a few (= not many, some) with plural countable nouns: We've got a few eggs. We use a little (= not much, some) with uncountable nouns: I want a little orange juice. Phrases of quantity: We use countable and uncountable nouns after phrases such as a jar/bottle/piece/loaf/cup/bar/glass/kilo/carton/bowl, etc.
exercises.instructionUz: 'Much' va 'many' savol va inkorda ishlatiladi. Much - sanalmaydigan otlar bilan, many - ko'plik sanaladigan otlar bilan: Qopda shakar ko'pmi? Qutida sut ko'p emas. Plastinkalaring ko'pmi? Uning do'stlari ko'p emas. 'A few' (= ko'p emas, bir nechta) - ko'plik sanaladigan otlar bilan: Bizda bir nechta tuxum bor. 'A little' (= ko'p emas, bir oz) - sanalmaydigan otlar bilan: Men bir oz apelsin sharbati xohlayman. Miqdor iboralari: a jar/bottle/piece/loaf/cup/bar/glass/kilo/carton/bowl va h.k. dan keyin sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar keladi.
exercises.explanationUz:
MIQDOR SO'ZLARI - SANALADIGANMI,
  SANALMAYDIGANMI?

  SANALADIGAN (ko'plik):  SANALMAYDIGAN:
    MANY records            MUCH sugar
    A FEW eggs              A LITTLE juice

  MUCH / MANY - savol va inkorda:
    Is there MUCH sugar in the
    bag?
    There isn't MUCH milk.
    Have you got MANY records?
    She hasn't got MANY friends.

  A FEW = bir nechta (ko'plik):
    We've got A FEW eggs.
  A LITTLE = bir oz (sanalmaydigan):
    I want A LITTLE orange juice.


MIQDOR IBORALARI (sanalmaydiganni
  sanash uchun):

  a JAR of jam (banka)
  a BOTTLE of water (shisha)
  a PIECE of cake (bo'lak)
  a LOAF of bread (bir buxanka)
  a CUP of tea (piyola)
  a BAR of chocolate (plitka)
  a GLASS of milk (stakan)
  a KILO of apples (kilo)
  a CARTON of juice (quti)
  a BOWL of soup (kosa)

exercises.instructionEn: We use should to say what the right/best thing to do is: You should eat plenty of fruit and vegetables. (= It's a good idea) We use shouldn't to say what isn't the right/best thing to do: You shouldn't eat junk food. (= It isn't a good idea)
exercises.instructionUz: 'Should' - to'g'ri/eng yaxshi ish nima ekanini aytish uchun: Siz ko'p meva-sabzavot yeyishingiz kerak. (= Bu yaxshi fikr) 'Shouldn't' - noto'g'ri ish nima ekanini aytish uchun: Siz zararli taom yemasligingiz kerak. (= Bu yaxshi fikr emas)
exercises.explanationUz:
SHOULD - MASLAHAT (... kerak).

  SHOULD + fe'l = qilish kerak
    (yaxshi fikr):
    You SHOULD eat plenty of fruit
    and vegetables.

  SHOULDN'T + fe'l = qilmaslik
    kerak (yomon fikr):
    You SHOULDN'T eat junk food.

  ⚠ Hamma shaxsda bir xil, 'to'
  yo'q: 'He should eats' ✗, 'should
  to eat' ✗.


⚠ 'PLENTY OF':

  = ko'p, yetarlicha.

points.en: You should eat plenty of fruit and vegetables. (= It's a good idea)
points.uz: Siz ko'p meva-sabzavot yeyishingiz kerak. (yaxshi fikr)

points.en: You shouldn't eat junk food. (= It isn't a good idea)
points.uz: Siz zararli taom yemasligingiz kerak. (yomon fikr)

exercises.instructionEn: Type 0 conditionals are used to express something which is always true. They are also used to talk about something which always happens as a result of something else: If + present simple → present simple: If the temperature falls below 0°C, water turns into ice. In type 0 conditionals we can use when (= whenever) instead of if: If/When the sun shines, snow melts. Time words: We do not use the future simple after the time words before, after, while, until, as soon as, and when. We use the present simple instead: I'll wait for you until you finish. (NOT: until you'll finish.) When can be followed by future simple if it is used as a question word: When will he arrive? I can't tell you when it will be ready. (when = question word) Please give me a call when you finish work. (when = time word)
exercises.instructionUz: 0-tur shart gap HAR DOIM TO'G'RI bo'lgan narsani bildiradi. Shuningdek, biror narsa natijasida har doim bo'ladigan narsa uchun: If + present simple → present simple: Agar harorat 0°C dan pastga tushsa, suv muzga aylanadi. 0-tur shart gapda 'if' o'rniga 'when' (= har safar) ishlatish mumkin: Quyosh chiqsa/chiqqanda, qor eriydi. Vaqt so'zlari: before, after, while, until, as soon as, when dan keyin future simple IShLATILMAYDI - present simple ishlatiladi: Tugatguningcha seni kutaman. (until you'll finish ✗) 'When' savol so'zi bo'lsa, keyin future simple kelishi mumkin: U qachon keladi? Qachon tayyor bo'lishini ayta olmayman. (when = savol so'zi) Ishni tugatganingda qo'ng'iroq qil. (when = vaqt so'zi)
exercises.explanationUz:
0-TUR ShART GAP - HAR DOIM TO'G'RI.

  IF + PRESENT SIMPLE, + PRESENT
  SIMPLE (ikkala qism ham!)

  If the temperature FALLS below
  0°C, water TURNS into ice.
  (tabiat qonuni - har doim)

  IF = WHEN (= whenever, har
  safar):
  If/When the sun SHINES, snow
  MELTS.

  ⚠ 1-TUR bilan FARQI:
  0-tur: har doim to'g'ri → present
  1-tur: kelajakdagi bir holat →
  will


VAQT SO'ZLARI - WILL YO'Q!

  before, after, while, until, as
  soon as, when dan keyin PRESENT
  SIMPLE:
  I'll wait for you UNTIL you
  FINISH. (until you'll finish ✗)

  ⚠ ISTISNO - 'when' SAVOL SO'ZI
  bo'lsa, will bo'ladi:
  WHEN WILL he arrive? (qachon?)
  I can't tell you WHEN it WILL be
  ready. (qachon - savol)
  LEKIN: Please give me a call
  WHEN you FINISH work. (vaqt
  so'zi - present)


⚠ 'TO MELT':

  = erimoq.


⚠ 'AS SOON AS':

  = ... bilanoq, ... zahoti.

points.en: If the temperature falls below 0°C, water turns into ice. (always true)
points.uz: Agar harorat 0°C dan pastga tushsa, suv muzga aylanadi. (har doim to'g'ri)

points.en: If/When the sun shines, snow melts. (when = whenever)
points.uz: Quyosh chiqsa/chiqqanda, qor eriydi. (when = har safar)

points.en: I'll wait for you until you finish. (NOT: until you'll finish)
When will he arrive? I can't tell you when it will be ready. (when = question word → future simple)
points.uz: U qachon keladi? Qachon tayyor bo'lishini ayta olmayman. (when - savol so'zi → will)

points.en: Please give me a call when you finish work. (when = time word → present simple)
points.uz: Ishni tugatganingda qo'ng'iroq qil. (when - vaqt so'zi → present)

patterns.formula: Would you like some ...? / Can I have some ...? / Have you got any ...? / There isn't any ...
patterns.exampleEn: Would you like some orange juice? Have you got any biscuits? There isn't any salt left.
patterns.exampleUz: Apelsin sharbati ichasizmi? Pechenye bormi? Tuz qolmagan.

patterns.formula: Is there much + SANALMAYDIGAN? / Have you got many + KO'PLIK?
patterns.exampleEn: Is there much sugar in the bag? Have you got many records?
You should eat plenty of fruit. You shouldn't eat junk food.
patterns.exampleUz: Ko'p meva yeyishingiz kerak. Zararli taom yemasligingiz kerak.

patterns.formula: If / When + KIM + FE'L(s), KIM + FE'L(s)
patterns.exampleEn: If the temperature falls below 0°C, water turns into ice.
patterns.exampleUz: Agar harorat 0°C dan pastga tushsa, suv muzga aylanadi.

patterns.formula: I'll + FE'L + until / when / as soon as + KIM + FE'L(s)
patterns.exampleEn: I'll wait for you until you finish. Please give me a call when you finish work.
patterns.exampleUz: Tugatguningcha seni kutaman. Ishni tugatganingda qo'ng'iroq qil.
